1.explanation: Both of these filters implement the logic that discovers and renders figures based on the presence of a caption. In common/figures.lua, `discoverFigure` (and related helpers) only returns an Image when `#image.caption > 0`, so an empty caption vector causes the image to be ignored. In quarto-pre/figures.lua the `Div` and `Para` handlers propagate `fig-cap` into the block content only when the attribute is non-nil, but an empty caption attribute ends up getting dropped before discoverFigure runs. Together these two files control how zero-length captions are handled, and must be updated to treat an empty caption value as “caption present but empty” rather than “no figure.”
1.bug_scenario: The reproducer shows two R code chunks in a Quarto document. The first chunk uses `#| fig-cap: !expr caption` with `caption <- "hello world"`, and correctly renders the image with the caption “hello world.” The second chunk sets `caption <- character(0)`, so the caption expression evaluates to a zero-length character vector. In this case the figure is dropped entirely from the HTML output – you don’t see the image or any placeholder. (The attached image is a stylized pencil sketch of two cartoon characters—one pony playing a keyboard and a Jigglypuff-like creature—each holding a microphone and singing.)
